_general.summary: Flutter interviews expect a solid model of widgets→elements→render objects, rebuild cost, and async BuildContext safety.
_general.problem: Treating Flutter like a DOM framework misses constraints, keys, and the UI-thread isolate model.
_general.mechanics: Explain the pipeline for the symptom (build/layout/paint), propose a minimal repro, then a fix with a widget test.
_general.tradeoffs: Prefer composition and framework APIs over fighting the engine with hacks.
_general.troubleshoot: Use DevTools timeline and inspector before guessing.
_general.integration: 1) Reproduce. 2) Identify pipeline stage. 3) Fix with keys/state/constraints. 4) Add widget test. 5) Verify in profile mode.

adaptive UI.summary: Adaptive UI selects platform-appropriate patterns (Material vs Cupertino, navigation idioms) while sharing logic.
adaptive UI.problem: Forcing Material everywhere on iOS feels foreign; duplicating entire apps is costly.
adaptive UI.mechanics: Share VMs/repos, branch widgets via Theme.of.platform or adaptive constructors, test both targets.
adaptive UI.tradeoffs: Adaptive takes effort; sometimes product chooses one design language deliberately.
adaptive UI.troubleshoot: If iOS back gesture breaks, navigation adaptation incomplete.
adaptive UI.integration: 1) Shared logic. 2) Adaptive widgets map. 3) Dual screenshots. 4) Platform QA checklist.

Android permissions.summary: Android permissions gate sensitive APIs; dangerous permissions require runtime requests on modern SDKs.
Android permissions.problem: Declaring only in manifest without runtime request fails on Android 6+.
Android permissions.mechanics: Declare in AndroidManifest, request at use-time with permission_handler, and degrade gracefully on deny.
Android permissions.tradeoffs: Ask too early and users deny permanently; ask in context of the feature.
Android permissions.troubleshoot: If permanently denied, deep-link to settings; verify merged manifest.
Android permissions.integration: 1) Inventory permissions. 2) Request in-context. 3) Handle denied. 4) Test across API levels. 5) Document why each is needed.

AnimationController.summary: AnimationController drives ticker-based animations with duration, vsync, and status listeners—usually owned by State.
AnimationController.problem: Controllers without disposal leak tickers; creating them in build resets animations.
AnimationController.mechanics: Create controller in initState with vsync: this, drive Tween/Animation, dispose in dispose().
AnimationController.tradeoffs: Explicit controllers give control vs implicit animations' simplicity.
AnimationController.troubleshoot: If assertion about ticker, missing SingleTickerProviderStateMixin or dispose.
AnimationController.example:
late final controller = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(ms: 300));
@override void dispose(){ controller.dispose(); super.dispose(); }
AnimationController.integration: 1) Mixin ticker provider. 2) Own controller in State. 3) Dispose. 4) Prefer ImplicitlyAnimated for simple cases.

APNs.summary: APNs (Apple Push Notification service) delivers remote notifications to iOS devices via device tokens and Apple's servers.
APNs.problem: Missing entitlements, wrong env (sandbox/prod), or expired certs/keys silently drop pushes.
APNs.mechanics: Register for notifications, send token to backend, authenticate to APNs with key, handle foreground/background differently.
APNs.tradeoffs: Keys are easier to rotate than certs; still need correct bundle id/topic.
APNs.troubleshoot: If undelivered, check token env mismatch and apns-topic.
APNs.example:
// iOS: capability Push Notifications + background modes as needed
// Backend: JWT ES256 to api.push.apple.com
APNs.integration: 1) Enable capability. 2) Capture tokens. 3) Backend APNs auth. 4) Test sandbox+prod. 5) Handle permission UX.

AppLifecycleState.summary: AppLifecycleState reports resumed/inactive/paused/detached/hidden so you can pause work and save state.
AppLifecycleState.problem: Ignoring lifecycle wastes battery with timers/sockets in background and loses draft state.
AppLifecycleState.mechanics: Add observer in initState, handle didChangeAppLifecycleState, remove observer on dispose.
AppLifecycleState.tradeoffs: Mobile OS may kill paused apps; persist critical state to disk, don't rely on memory.
AppLifecycleState.troubleshoot: If observer never fires, not registered or removed too early.
AppLifecycleState.integration: 1) Observe lifecycle. 2) Pause streams/timers. 3) Persist drafts. 4) Resume carefully. 5) Test backgrounding.

async BuildContext safety.summary: After an await, the State may be disposed—using BuildContext then asserts/crashes unless mounted is checked.
async BuildContext safety.problem: Fire-and-forget async in State without guards is a top Flutter crash source.
async BuildContext safety.mechanics: Await, then if (!mounted) return; before context use; or capture ScaffoldMessenger/Navigator before gap.
async BuildContext safety.tradeoffs: Lint catches many cases; still design cancellation for long tasks.
async BuildContext safety.troubleshoot: Enable use_build_context_synchronously and fix all hits.
async BuildContext safety.integration: 1) Enable lint. 2) mounted checks. 3) Cancel futures/subs on dispose. 4) Tests covering fast pop.

background task execution.summary: Background tasks run work when UI is not foreground—constrained heavily by iOS/Android policies.
background task execution.problem: Assuming infinite background CPU gets apps suspended/killed and store-rejected.
background task execution.mechanics: Use platform-supported schedulers, keep work short, persist progress, and test OS-kill scenarios.
background task execution.tradeoffs: Push-driven work often more reliable than frequent polling background fetches.
background task execution.troubleshoot: If never runs, missing native registration/permissions/Info.plist keys.
background task execution.example: // workmanager / flutter_background_fetch per platform setup docs
background task execution.integration: 1) Pick supported API. 2) Native setup. 3) Idempotent tasks. 4) Telemetry. 5) Store compliance review.

BLoC/Cubit.summary: BLoC/Cubit separate events/state from UI: Cubit exposes functions; BLoC maps events to states via streams.
BLoC/Cubit.problem: setState sprawl across the tree makes business logic untestable and rebuilds chaotic.
BLoC/Cubit.mechanics: Put logic in Cubit/Bloc, provide above subtree, rebuild with builders, navigate/side effects in listeners.
BLoC/Cubit.tradeoffs: BLoC ceremony helps large teams; Cubit is lighter for simple state. Don't Bloc everything.
BLoC/Cubit.troubleshoot: If UI misses states, check equality (Equatable) and buildWhen.
BLoC/Cubit.integration: 1) Introduce Cubit for a feature. 2) Provide at route. 3) Test cubit pure. 4) Listeners for side effects. 5) Avoid UI logic in widgets.

build phase.summary: The build phase runs Widget.build to produce a new widget configuration for dirty elements.
build phase.problem: Side effects in build (HTTP, setState) create loops and unpredictable UI.
build phase.mechanics: Keep build pure, trigger changes via events/setState outside build, and split widgets to limit rebuild scope.
build phase.tradeoffs: Rebuilds are normal; expensive builds are the problem.
build phase.troubleshoot: If infinite rebuild, setState during build—remove it.
build phase.example:
// Bad: build(){ setState((){}); }
// Good: derive UI from state fields only
build phase.integration: 1) Ban side effects in build. 2) Split widgets. 3) const. 4) Rebuild profiler.

BuildContext.summary: BuildContext is a handle to a widget's location in the tree—used to find InheritedWidgets, navigate, and theme.
BuildContext.problem: Using a context across async gaps after dispose, or the wrong context for Provider/Navigator, causes crashes/lookups to fail.
BuildContext.mechanics: Use context only when mounted; capture Navigator/Theme before await or check mounted after; prefer the context that can see the ancestor you need.
BuildContext.tradeoffs: Passing context deep is fine; storing it long-term is not. Element APIs are advanced.
BuildContext.troubleshoot: If 'deactivated widget' asserts, you used context after dispose—guard with mounted.
BuildContext.integration: 1) Audit async methods. 2) mounted checks. 3) Correct lookup context. 4) Widget tests for async nav.

BuildOwner.summary: BuildOwner schedules and manages the build pipeline for dirty Elements in the framework.
BuildOwner.problem: Misunderstanding who marks dirty leads to wrong optimization attempts outside the framework.
BuildOwner.mechanics: Widgets call setState → element marks dirty → BuildOwner rebuilds in frame; you rarely touch BuildOwner directly.
BuildOwner.tradeoffs: Framework internals help debugging; app code should stay at widget/state layer.
BuildOwner.troubleshoot: If infinite rebuilds, something marks dirty every build—find the setState loop.
BuildOwner.example: // Prefer fixing setState loops over hacking BuildOwner
BuildOwner.integration: 1) Use DevTools rebuild profiler. 2) Fix dirty loops. 3) Keep custom RenderObjects rare. 4) Read framework only when needed.

certificate pinning.summary: Certificate pinning trusts only specific certs/public keys for your API, mitigating rogue CAs/MITM on hostile networks.
certificate pinning.problem: No pinning still relies on system CAs; pinning without rotation plan bricks apps when certs expire.
certificate pinning.mechanics: Pin SPKI hashes in HTTP client, ship backup pins, and rotate ahead of expiry.
certificate pinning.tradeoffs: Security vs operational risk—often for higher threat apps; consider at TLS terminator carefully.
certificate pinning.troubleshoot: If prod suddenly fails TLS, pins outdated—roll emergency build with new pins.
certificate pinning.example: // dio HttpClientAdapter with SecurityContext / badCertificateCallback carefully pinned
certificate pinning.integration: 1) Decide threat model. 2) Pin+backup. 3) Rotation calendar. 4) Monitor TLS failures. 5) Emergency override process.

Cloud Firestore.summary: Cloud Firestore is a document/collection NoSQL DB with realtime listeners and offline persistence popular with Flutter apps.
Cloud Firestore.problem: Chatty listeners and unbounded queries explode reads/cost; poor modeling makes queries impossible.
Cloud Firestore.mechanics: Model for queries, add composite indexes, listen with streams, and enforce security rules—never trust client alone.
Cloud Firestore.tradeoffs: Realtime convenience vs cost/vendor lock-in; sometimes REST+SQL is simpler.
Cloud Firestore.troubleshoot: If missing index errors, create suggested composite index; audit read counts.
Cloud Firestore.integration: 1) Design collections. 2) Rules. 3) Indexes. 4) Limit listeners. 5) Monitor usage.

CocoaPods.summary: CocoaPods manages native iOS dependencies for Flutter plugins via the Podfile in ios/.
CocoaPods.problem: Pod version conflicts and outdated repos break `pod install` and iOS builds.
CocoaPods.mechanics: Run flutter pub get, cd ios && pod install, keep platform version compatible with plugins.
CocoaPods.tradeoffs: SwiftPM is emerging; many Flutter plugins still expect CocoaPods.
CocoaPods.troubleshoot: If install fails, update repo, clear Pods/Podfile.lock carefully, check minimum iOS version.
CocoaPods.example: cd ios && pod repo update && pod install
CocoaPods.integration: 1) Pin iOS platform. 2) Commit Podfile.lock. 3) CI pod install. 4) Document plugin native requirements.

code signing/provisioning.summary: iOS code signing binds apps to teams via certificates/profiles; Android uses keystores for package identity.
code signing/provisioning.problem: Wrong profiles/expired certs fail install/TestFlight; lost Android upload keys are catastrophic.
code signing/provisioning.mechanics: Automate signing with fastlane match or store keys in CI secrets; back up Android keystores.
code signing/provisioning.tradeoffs: Automation reduces pain; still need access control for signing material.
code signing/provisioning.troubleshoot: If 'provisioning profile doesn't include signing certificate', regenerate profiles.
code signing/provisioning.example:
fastlane match appstore
# Android: keep upload keystore in secret manager
code signing/provisioning.integration: 1) Centralize signing. 2) Backup keys. 3) CI inject. 4) Rotate Apple certs deliberately. 5) Document restore.

Codemagic/GitHub Actions.summary: CI systems like Codemagic and GitHub Actions build, test, and sign Flutter apps on every change.
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.problem: Manual local releases drift signing configs and skip tests.
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.mechanics: Run analyze/test, build IPA/AAB with secrets, cache Flutter/pub, and upload artifacts.
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.tradeoffs: Codemagic is Flutter-focused; GHA is flexible. Choose based on team familiarity and macOS minute costs.
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.troubleshoot: If signing fails in CI only, check provisioning secrets and keychain unlock steps.
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.example:
# GHA sketch
- uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
- run: flutter test && flutter build appbundle
Codemagic/GitHub Actions.integration: 1) Add CI workflow. 2) Cache deps. 3) Store signing secrets. 4) Gate merges on tests. 5) Automate store upload carefully.

compositing.summary: Compositing combines layers (often GPU) into final frames; opacity/clip/transform can create layers.
compositing.problem: Accidental saveLayer/opacity over large areas burns GPU fill rate.
compositing.mechanics: Reduce offscreen saves, prefer simpler effects, and profile raster jank.
compositing.tradeoffs: Pretty effects vs battery/GPU—measure on mid devices.
compositing.troubleshoot: If raster thread long, simplify blur/opacity/clips.
compositing.example: // Avoid Opacity wrapping huge lists; prefer fading smaller subtrees
compositing.integration: 1) Profile raster. 2) Reduce saveLayer. 3) Boundary wisely. 4) Test low-end Android.

CustomPainter.summary: CustomPainter draws via Canvas in a paint method—ideal for charts, game sprites, and custom shapes.
CustomPainter.problem: Heavy paint without shouldRepaint optimization janks scrolling; hit testing needs extra work.
CustomPainter.mechanics: Implement painter, wrap in CustomPaint, return true from shouldRepaint only when data changes.
CustomPainter.tradeoffs: Painter is powerful but accessibility/semantics need manual Semantics; prefer widgets when possible.
CustomPainter.troubleshoot: If always repainting, shouldRepaint always true—compare fields.
CustomPainter.integration: 1) Prototype with CustomPaint. 2) Optimize shouldRepaint. 3) Add semantics. 4) Profile. 5) Extract package if reused.

CustomScrollView and slivers.summary: Slivers are scrollable-area protocols; CustomScrollView composes slivers (lists, grids, app bars) in one scroll.
CustomScrollView and slivers.problem: Nested ListViews with their own scrolls fight; pinned headers need slivers.
CustomScrollView and slivers.mechanics: Compose slivers in CustomScrollView, use builders for laziness, and keep one primary scroll.
CustomScrollView and slivers.tradeoffs: Slivers are flexible but denser API than ListView; worth it for advanced scroll UI.
CustomScrollView and slivers.troubleshoot: If shrinkWrap perf issues, you forced unbounded work—use slivers instead.
CustomScrollView and slivers.integration: 1) Replace nested scrolls with slivers. 2) Lazy builders. 3) Pinned headers. 4) Test scroll performance.

Dart FFI.summary: Dart FFI calls native C APIs from Dart without channels—useful for shared libraries and performance-critical code.
Dart FFI.problem: Unsafe pointers and wrong ABI cause crashes outside Dart's usual safety.
Dart FFI.mechanics: Load library, bind signatures with ffi, manage memory carefully, and isolate heavy native work if needed.
Dart FFI.tradeoffs: FFI is fast and direct but platform packaging and safety are harder than Pigeon/channels for simple APIs.
Dart FFI.troubleshoot: If segfaults, audit lifetimes and struct sizes/alignment.
Dart FFI.example: final nativeAdd = lib.lookupFunction<Int32 Function(Int32, Int32), int Function(int, int)>('add');
Dart FFI.integration: 1) Identify C API need. 2) Bind via ffi. 3) Harden memory. 4) Test per ABI. 5) Document packaging.

Dart type system.summary: Dart's type system is sound with null safety, generics, and strong inference guiding safe refactors.
Dart type system.problem: Dynamic sprawl and bang operators (!) hide null bugs until runtime.
Dart type system.mechanics: Type APIs explicitly, prefer nullable modeling over !, and enable strict analysis options.
Dart type system.tradeoffs: Strictness slows some prototyping but pays off in large apps.
Dart type system.troubleshoot: If analyzer disagrees with runtime, you cast incorrectly—remove casts.
Dart type system.integration: 1) Enable strict analysis. 2) Remove dynamic. 3) Model nulls. 4) Fix analyzer issues in CI.

debug/profile/release modes.summary: Flutter has debug (asserts/JIT), profile (performance-like with tooling), and release (optimized AOT) modes.
debug/profile/release modes.problem: Judging jank in debug mode misleads—debug is slower by design.
debug/profile/release modes.mechanics: Develop in debug, measure in profile, ship release; never quote debug FPS as truth.
debug/profile/release modes.tradeoffs: Profile close to release but not identical; still verify release builds.
debug/profile/release modes.troubleshoot: If 'only release crashes', minify/strip issue—test release locally.
debug/profile/release modes.integration: 1) Educate team on modes. 2) Perf only in profile. 3) QA release builds. 4) Keep asserts for debug checks.

deep linking.summary: Deep links open specific app routes from URLs (App Links/Universal Links/custom schemes).
deep linking.problem: Misconfigured intent filters/apple-app-site-association breaks links into browser-only.
deep linking.mechanics: Claim domains, configure platform files, parse URIs into routes, and test install/referrer flows.
deep linking.tradeoffs: Verified HTTPS links are better UX/security than custom schemes alone.
deep linking.troubleshoot: If links open site not app, assetlinks/AASA or intent filters wrong.
deep linking.example: // Android intent-filter + assetlinks.json; iOS associated domains
deep linking.integration: 1) Domain verify. 2) Platform config. 3) Router parse. 4) Cold/warm tests. 5) Analytics on link opens.

dependency injection.summary: DI supplies collaborators (repos/clients) to widgets/VMs instead of constructing globals everywhere.
dependency injection.problem: Singletons and `new` in widgets make testing and swapping environments painful.
dependency injection.mechanics: Register implementations at startup, inject into VMs, override fakes in tests.
dependency injection.tradeoffs: Service locators are convenient but hide dependencies; constructor DI is clearer when practical.
dependency injection.troubleshoot: If wrong impl in tests, registration order/overrides missing.
dependency injection.integration: 1) Choose DI approach. 2) Register at boot. 3) Inject VMs. 4) Test overrides. 5) Env flavors.

design tokens.summary: Design tokens are named raw values (color/space/type) shared between design and Flutter Theme.
design tokens.problem: Magic numbers diverge from Figma and break dark theme consistency.
design tokens.mechanics: Map tokens into ThemeData/ThemeExtension and reference tokens in widgets only.
design tokens.tradeoffs: Heavy token systems need discipline; start with color/space/type.
design tokens.troubleshoot: If dark mode misses, token not mapped through ColorScheme/extension.
design tokens.integration: 1) Extract tokens. 2) ThemeExtension. 3) Replace magic numbers. 4) Sync with design. 5) Contrast checks.

DevTools performance timeline.summary: DevTools Performance timeline shows UI/Raster thread frames to diagnose jank sources.
DevTools performance timeline.problem: Guessing optimizations without frames data wastes time.
DevTools performance timeline.mechanics: Run profile mode, record interaction, inspect timeline, fix rebuilds/layout/shaders accordingly.
DevTools performance timeline.tradeoffs: Debug mode is not representative—always profile in profile/release.
DevTools performance timeline.troubleshoot: If UI thread long, reduce build; if raster, simplify effects/images.
DevTools performance timeline.example:
flutter run --profile
# open DevTools → Performance → record
DevTools performance timeline.integration: 1) Profile mode. 2) Record jank. 3) Attribute UI/Raster. 4) Fix. 5) Re-measure.

Drift.summary: Drift (moor) is a reactive Dart ORM over SQLite with type-safe queries and streams of changes.
Drift.problem: Raw sqflite SQL strings drift from models and miss reactive UI updates.
Drift.mechanics: Define tables, generate code, watch selects as streams, migrate schema versions carefully.
Drift.tradeoffs: Codegen improves safety but adds build_runner complexity.
Drift.troubleshoot: If stream not updating, query not watched or transaction isolation unexpected.
Drift.integration: 1) Add Drift. 2) Define tables. 3) Migrations. 4) watch() in UI. 5) Test DAO.

Element tree.summary: The Element tree is Flutter's mutable realization of Widgets—holding State, managing mounts, and configuring RenderObjects.
Element tree.problem: Confusing Widget rebuilds with Element remounts leads to wrong key/state diagnoses.
Element tree.mechanics: Framework matches widgets to elements by runtimeType+key; updates reuse elements; type/key changes remount.
Element tree.tradeoffs: You rarely create Elements manually; understanding them debugs keys/state bugs.
Element tree.troubleshoot: If State resets, Element remounted—inspect keys/types in inspector.
Element tree.example: // Changing Key or widget type at a slot remounts Element/State
Element tree.integration: 1) Teach three trees. 2) Fix keys. 3) Use inspector. 4) Add tests for state retention.

event loop and microtask queue.summary: Dart's event loop runs microtasks before the next event events; UI frame callbacks interleave with events.
event loop and microtask queue.problem: Scheduling endless microtasks can starve frames similarly to JS.
event loop and microtask queue.mechanics: Know await scheduling, use Future for yielding to events, and keep frame callbacks short.
event loop and microtask queue.tradeoffs: Same lessons as web event loops—apply to isolates' loops.
event loop and microtask queue.troubleshoot: If UI starves with tiny tasks, microtask storm—batch/yield.
event loop and microtask queue.integration: 1) Teach ordering. 2) Avoid microtask storms. 3) Profile frames. 4) Move CPU to isolates.

Expanded.summary: Expanded is a Flex child that forces a child to consume remaining space along the main axis (flex fit tight).
Expanded.problem: Putting Expanded outside Row/Column/Flex throws; unbounded flex parents fail layout.
Expanded.mechanics: Wrap children in Expanded/Flexible inside Row/Column to distribute leftover space.
Expanded.tradeoffs: Expanded is convenient; sometimes Align/SizedBox is clearer for fixed layouts.
Expanded.troubleshoot: If 'Incorrect use of ParentDataWidget', Expanded isn't under Flex.
Expanded.integration: 1) Use Expanded for leftover space. 2) Prefer Flexible for not-forced fill. 3) Fix unbounded lists separately.

extension methods.summary: Dart extensions add methods/getters to existing types without altering them—great for UI helpers.
extension methods.problem: Overusing extensions hides where APIs live and can collide names.
extension methods.mechanics: Create focused extensions (e.g., on BuildContext for theme), import deliberately.
extension methods.tradeoffs: Nice DX vs discoverability—document team extensions.
extension methods.troubleshoot: If extension missing, import not in scope.
extension methods.integration: 1) Add curated extensions. 2) Lint collisions. 3) Document. 4) Avoid business logic in extensions.

FCM.summary: Firebase Cloud Messaging routes push notifications to Android/iOS/web clients with topics and device tokens.
FCM.problem: Missing platform setup (APNs key, google-services) means tokens never receive messages.
FCM.mechanics: Integrate firebase_messaging, collect tokens, handle background isolates, and send via FCM HTTP v1.
FCM.tradeoffs: FCM simplifies cross-platform push but ties you to Google infrastructure.
FCM.troubleshoot: If iOS silent fails, check APNs key in Firebase console and background modes.
FCM.integration: 1) Platform setup. 2) Token pipeline. 3) Handlers. 4) Topic strategy. 5) Test killed/background/foreground.

federated plugin architecture.summary: Federated plugins split app-facing API, platform interface, and platform implementations into packages.
federated plugin architecture.problem: Monolithic plugins make contributions and multi-platform support harder.
federated plugin architecture.mechanics: Follow Flutter federated layout, implement platform interface, and endorse impls in pubspec.
federated plugin architecture.tradeoffs: More packages to version; clearer ownership and testing.
federated plugin architecture.troubleshoot: If wrong impl resolves, endorsements/pubspec miswired.
federated plugin architecture.integration: 1) Split plugin. 2) Platform interface. 3) CI per platform. 4) Versioning policy. 5) Example app.

final and const.summary: final means single-assignment; const means compile-time constant canonicalized values—key for Flutter perf.
final and const.problem: Missing const on widgets forces rebuild work that could be reused.
final and const.mechanics: Prefer final fields, const widgets/constructors deeply when values are compile-time constant.
final and const.tradeoffs: Const is great; not everything can be const (depends on runtime).
final and const.troubleshoot: If analyzer suggests const, take it unless it harms readability badly.
final and const.integration: 1) Prefer final. 2) Const widgets. 3) Lint prefer_const. 4) Review hot paths.

Firebase Auth.summary: Firebase Auth provides managed identity (email, social, anonymous) with ID tokens for securing backends.
Firebase Auth.problem: Rolling your own auth incorrectly stores passwords badly and breaks multi-platform sessions.
Firebase Auth.mechanics: Sign in via plugin, listen authStateChanges, attach tokens to API calls, and gate Firestore rules by uid.
Firebase Auth.tradeoffs: Fast to ship vs vendor lock-in and limited enterprise IdP needs.
Firebase Auth.troubleshoot: If rules deny, print token claims and compare uid paths.
Firebase Auth.integration: 1) Enable providers. 2) Wire auth stream. 3) Secure rules/API. 4) Persist session. 5) Handle account linking.

flavors and dart-define.summary: Flavors/schemas and --dart-define configure app ids, icons, and compile-time env (API URLs) per variant.
flavors and dart-define.problem: Hard-coded prod URLs in debug cause accidents; manual switching is error-prone.
flavors and dart-define.mechanics: Define flavors, pass dart-defines for env, and separate applicationIds/bundle ids.
flavors and dart-define.tradeoffs: More flavors increase CI matrix cost—keep to needed envs.
flavors and dart-define.troubleshoot: If wrong API hit, define not passed in IDE run config.
flavors and dart-define.integration: 1) Define flavors. 2) dart-define env. 3) IDE configs. 4) CI matrix. 5) Distinct app ids.

Flutter constraints model.summary: Flutter layout is constraints down, sizes up: parents pass BoxConstraints, children choose a size within them.
Flutter constraints model.problem: Fighting constraints with unbounded children (ListView in Column without Expanded) causes overflow/assert.
Flutter constraints model.mechanics: Read incoming constraints, size child, parent positions; use Expanded/SizedBox.expand intentionally.
Flutter constraints model.tradeoffs: Model is consistent once learned; coming from CSS requires unlearning some habits.
Flutter constraints model.troubleshoot: If yellow/black stripes, overflow—inspect constraints in DevTools.
Flutter constraints model.integration: 1) Learn constraints. 2) Fix unbounded scrollables. 3) Use Inspector. 4) Document layout patterns.

Flutter desktop windowing.summary: Flutter desktop manages native windows/menus/multi-window with platform channels and windowing plugins.
Flutter desktop windowing.problem: Mobile-first layouts break on large resizable windows without adaptive breakpoints.
Flutter desktop windowing.mechanics: Handle resize, provide desktop navigation patterns, and test macOS/Windows/Linux targets.
Flutter desktop windowing.tradeoffs: One codebase helps but desktop UX expectations differ—budget polish.
Flutter desktop windowing.troubleshoot: If content clipped, missing responsive layout for wide windows.
Flutter desktop windowing.integration: 1) Enable desktop targets. 2) Adaptive layout. 3) Shortcuts/menus. 4) CI per OS. 5) Polish window states.

Flutter Web rendering.summary: Flutter web can render via CanvasKit/Skwasm or HTML backends with different perf and download costs.
Flutter Web rendering.problem: Shipping huge CanvasKit wasm without need hurts first load on slow networks.
Flutter Web rendering.mechanics: Choose renderer for app needs, optimize asset sizes, and understand SEO/text selection differences vs DOM apps.
Flutter Web rendering.tradeoffs: Flutter web is great for app-like UIs; content sites often better as HTML frameworks.
Flutter Web rendering.troubleshoot: If first load huge, analyze CanvasKit size and deferred imports.
Flutter Web rendering.integration: 1) Pick renderer. 2) Measure TTI. 3) Optimize assets. 4) Decide SEO strategy. 5) Test browsers.

Focus system.summary: Flutter's focus system manages keyboard/traversal focus via FocusNode/FocusScope for accessibility and shortcuts.
Focus system.problem: Custom controls without focus nodes are unreachable via keyboard.
Focus system.mechanics: Attach Focus widgets/nodes, define traversal order, and show focus highlights.
Focus system.tradeoffs: Framework defaults work for many Material widgets; custom painters need manual focus.
Focus system.troubleshoot: If Tab skips controls, missing focus nodes or incorrect scopes.
Focus system.example:
final node = FocusNode();
Focus(focusNode: node, child: ...);
Focus system.integration: 1) Audit keyboard nav. 2) Add FocusNodes. 3) Visible indicators. 4) Tests with sendKeyEvent. 5) Dispose nodes.

foreground/background services.summary: Android foreground services run user-visible ongoing work; background services are heavily restricted post-O/12+.
foreground/background services.problem: Starting background work illegally gets killed or Play policy strikes.
foreground/background services.mechanics: Use FGS with proper type/notification when required; prefer WorkManager for deferrable tasks.
foreground/background services.tradeoffs: FGS UX cost (persistent notification) vs reliability.
foreground/background services.troubleshoot: If killed immediately, missing notification/type or policy violation.
foreground/background services.example: // flutter_foreground_task / native FGS with type + notification channel
foreground/background services.integration: 1) Confirm need. 2) Correct FGS type. 3) Notification UX. 4) Play policy review. 5) Prefer deferred work when possible.

Form validation.summary: Flutter Form/FormField widgets collect validators and validate() before submit with a FormState key.
Form validation.problem: Creating a new GlobalKey every build resets FormState and loses field state.
Form validation.mechanics: Keep one Form key in State, validate on submit, show errors, and keep field controllers disposed.
Form validation.tradeoffs: Form widget is fine for simple forms; complex flows may use separate state management.
Form validation.troubleshoot: If validators never run, you didn't call formKey.currentState?.validate().
Form validation.integration: 1) Stable Form key. 2) Validators. 3) Dispose controllers. 4) Widget tests. 5) Server-side validate too.

frame lifecycle.summary: A Flutter frame walks build → layout → paint → composite on UI/raster threads targeting ~16ms.
frame lifecycle.problem: Work exceeding budget drops frames and feels janky.
frame lifecycle.mechanics: Keep per-frame work small, defer heavy tasks, and profile timeline.
frame lifecycle.tradeoffs: Some jank is shader/IO—not always your Dart code.
frame lifecycle.troubleshoot: Attribute jank via DevTools before optimizing.
frame lifecycle.integration: 1) Understand phases. 2) Profile. 3) Cut build/layout/paint costs. 4) Defer non-critical work.

Freezed.summary: Freezed generates immutable union/data classes with copyWith, equality, and pattern matching helpers.
Freezed.problem: Hand-written ==/hashCode and mutable models cause subtle state bugs in BLoC/Cubit.
Freezed.mechanics: Annotate classes, run build_runner, emit states as freezed unions, and switch exhaustively.
Freezed.tradeoffs: Codegen DX is great; build times and generated noise are the cost.
Freezed.troubleshoot: If equality always fails, forgot freezed annotation/codegen.
Freezed.integration: 1) Add freezed. 2) Model states. 3) Generate. 4) Exhaustive switches. 5) CI codegen check.

Future.summary: A Future represents a single async result in Dart—completed with a value or error.
Future.problem: Unawaited futures hide errors; using BuildContext after await without mounted checks crashes.
Future.mechanics: Await futures, handle errors with try/catch or catchError, and parallelize with Future.wait when independent.
Future.tradeoffs: Futures are one-shot; Streams are for multi-event. Don't convert everything to streams.
Future.troubleshoot: If errors disappear, you forgot await/catch—use unawaited_lints.
Future.integration: 1) Lint unawaited futures. 2) mounted after await. 3) Parallelize carefully. 4) Surface errors to UI.

garbage collection.summary: Dart GC reclaims unreachable objects; GC pauses can contribute to jank if allocation rates are huge.
garbage collection.problem: Allocating large temporary graphs every frame increases GC frequency.
garbage collection.mechanics: Reduce per-frame allocations, cancel listeners, and inspect memory graphs for leaks.
garbage collection.troubleshoot: If memory climbs across routes, leaked listeners/GlobalKeys/streams.
garbage collection.example: // DevTools Memory → take heap snapshot, compare
garbage collection.integration: 1) Snapshot before/after flows. 2) Fix leaks. 3) Reduce hot-path allocs. 4) Re-profile frames.

generics.summary: Dart generics parameterize classes/functions for type-safe collections and APIs.
generics.problem: Using dynamic lists loses safety and forces casts.
concepts: reified generics vs Java erasure differences
generics.mechanics: Type public APIs, constrain parameters, and let inference work locally.
generics.tradeoffs: Same tradeoffs as other languages—clarity over cleverness.
generics.integration: 1) Generic repos/APIs. 2) Avoid dynamic. 3) Analyzer strictness. 4) Examples in docs.

GlobalKey.summary: GlobalKey uniquely identifies an element across the tree—used for FormState and rare reparenting cases.
GlobalKey.problem: Creating GlobalKeys in build is expensive and resets state; overuse is a smell.
GlobalKey.mechanics: Store GlobalKey in State fields, access currentState sparingly, prefer ValueKey for list identity.
GlobalKey.tradeoffs: Powerful but breaks encapsulation; avoid for routine list keys.
GlobalKey.troubleshoot: If Form resets each rebuild, GlobalKey was recreated in build.
GlobalKey.example: final formKey = GlobalKey<FormState>(); // field on State, not in build
GlobalKey.integration: 1) Ban GlobalKey in build. 2) Use for Form/Scaffold rarely. 3) Prefer ValueKey. 4) Review PRs for misuse.

go_router.summary: go_router implements Router API with declarative routes, deep links, redirects, and nested navigation.
go_router.problem: Imperative Navigator-only apps struggle with web URLs and complex auth redirects.
go_router.mechanics: Declare route table, redirect for auth, nest shells, and parse deep links.
go_router.tradeoffs: Declarative routing helps; migration from Navigator 1.0 takes care for results/pop.
go_router.troubleshoot: If redirect loops, conditions overlap—add logging.
go_router.integration: 1) Adopt go_router. 2) Auth redirect. 3) Deep link test. 4) Nested shells. 5) Analytics observer.

golden test.summary: Golden tests screenshot widgets and compare against committed baseline images for visual regressions.
golden test.problem: Text/layout bugs escape behavior tests but get caught by goldens.
golden test.mechanics: Pump widget, expect later matching golden, update with flag when intentional.
golden test.tradeoffs: Goldens flake across OS fonts if not controlled; use consistent CI images.
golden test.troubleshoot: If local/CI differ, font/rendering variance—standardize CI container.
golden test.integration: 1) Add goldens for key UI. 2) Lock CI fonts. 3) Review updates in PR. 4) Keep set small/high value.

Gradle/AGP compatibility.summary: Android builds require compatible Gradle, Android Gradle Plugin, Kotlin, and JDK versions with Flutter's templates.
Gradle/AGP compatibility.problem: Random upgrades break builds with cryptic AGP/Gradle mismatch errors.
Gradle/AGP compatibility.mechanics: Follow Flutter's supported matrix, upgrade via flutter create repair/docs, and change versions together.
Gradle/AGP compatibility.tradeoffs: Staying current gets Play requirements; bleeding edge breaks plugins.
Gradle/AGP compatibility.troubleshoot: If build fails after upgrade, read compatibility table and align wrapper+AGP+Kotlin.
Gradle/AGP compatibility.example: // android/build.gradle AGP version must match gradle-wrapper.properties
Gradle/AGP compatibility.integration: 1) Track Flutter Android upgrade guides. 2) Upgrade in lockstep. 3) CI on clean checkout. 4) Pin versions.

Hero animation.summary: Hero widgets animate a shared-tag element between routes during Navigator transitions.
Hero animation.problem: Duplicate tags in one route or missing pairs cause jumps instead of flights.
Hero animation.mechanics: Wrap shared visuals with matching Hero tags on both routes; keep tags unique within a route.
Hero animation.tradeoffs: Heroes delight but can conflict with complex custom transitions.
Hero animation.troubleshoot: If two heroes conflict, tags collide—make tags include ids.
Hero animation.integration: 1) Identify shared elements. 2) Matching tags. 3) Unique per route. 4) Test transitions. 5) Disable if a11y prefers reduced motion.

hit testing.summary: Hit testing determines which render object receives a pointer event by walking the hit test tree.
hit testing.problem: Ignoring pointers incorrectly or deferring hits breaks taps on overlapping UIs.
hit testing.mechanics: Use IgnorePointer/AbsorbPointer intentionally, set behavior on listeners, and verify overlapping targets.
hit testing.tradeoffs: Custom hit shapes need RenderBox.hitTest overrides—rare.
hit testing.troubleshoot: If taps pass through, IgnorePointer or behavior translucent issues.
hit testing.integration: 1) Define overlay intent. 2) Absorb/Ignore correctly. 3) Widget tests taps. 4) Custom hits only if needed.

http package.summary: The http package is Dart's simple HTTP client API for REST calls.
http package.problem: Forgetting timeouts/headers and parsing without status checks causes hangs and silent failures.
http package.mechanics: Create a shared Client, set timeouts via IOClient/adapters if needed, check status, close clients.
http package.tradeoffs: http is minimal; dio adds interceptors—standardize one.
http package.troubleshoot: If sockets leak, Client not closed.
http package.example:
final client = http.Client();
try { final res = await client.get(url); } finally { client.close(); }
http package.integration: 1) Shared client. 2) Status checks. 3) Timeouts. 4) Interceptors/auth layer. 5) Tests with MockClient.

image memory management.summary: Image memory can dominate Flutter RAM; cache width/height and eviction matter for galleries.
image memory management.problem: Decoding full-res images into thumbnails OOMs on low-end devices.
image memory management.mechanics: Provide decode sizes for display size, clear caches on memory warnings if needed, and dispose controllers.
image memory management.tradeoffs: Quality vs memory—decode near display pixel size.
image memory management.troubleshoot: If OOM in gallery, missing cacheWidth—add it.
image memory management.integration: 1) Decode near display size. 2) Limit cache. 3) Profile memory. 4) Paginate galleries. 5) Test low-end Android.

Impeller rendering.summary: Impeller is Flutter's modern renderer aiming for predictable performance by precompiling shaders (esp. iOS).
Impeller rendering.problem: Skia runtime shader compilation caused first-animation jank on iOS.
Impeller rendering.mechanics: Use current Flutter channels where Impeller is default/enabled, profile animations, and report gaps.
Impeller rendering.tradeoffs: Impeller improves jank but may lag some rare Skia effects—verify your app.
Impeller rendering.troubleshoot: If visual bugs, try disabling Impeller to compare and file issues.
Impeller rendering.example: flutter run --enable-impeller  # or disable per docs when debugging
Impeller rendering.integration: 1) Upgrade Flutter. 2) Profile animations. 3) Validate visuals. 4) Keep repros for engine bugs.

implicit animations.summary: Implicit animations (AnimatedContainer/Opacity/etc.) tween property changes without manual controllers.
implicit animations.problem: Using explicit controllers for simple property changes adds boilerplate and leak risk.
implicit animations.mechanics: Change target fields in state; implicit widgets animate to new values automatically.
implicit animations.tradeoffs: Simple UX wins; complex sequenced animations need AnimationController.
implicit animations.troubleshoot: If no animation, you replaced widget type/key remounting instead of updating props.
implicit animations.example: AnimatedContainer(duration: Duration(ms: 200), color: selected ? Colors.teal : Colors.grey);
implicit animations.integration: 1) Prefer implicit for simple. 2) Keep keys stable. 3) Escalate to explicit when sequencing. 4) Respect reduced motion.

InheritedWidget.summary: InheritedWidget efficiently broadcasts data downward; dependents rebuild when updateShouldNotify says so.
InheritedWidget.problem: Recreating inherited values every build without notification control causes broad rebuilds—or none when needed.
InheritedWidget.mechanics: Expose static of(context), call context.dependOn..., and implement updateShouldNotify by value compare.
InheritedWidget.tradeoffs: Low-level vs Provider/Riverpod convenience—know it to debug.
InheritedWidget.troubleshoot: If child doesn't rebuild, updateShouldNotify false or not dependent (used context incorrectly).
InheritedWidget.integration: 1) Use for true ambient data. 2) Correct of(context). 3) Notify carefully. 4) Prefer community libs for app state.

integration test.summary: integration_test drives the full app on device/emulator for end-to-end Flutter flows.
integration test.problem: Relying only on widget tests misses plugin/channel and performance issues.
integration test.mechanics: Write integration tests for critical journeys, run on CI devices, reset state between tests.
integration test.troubleshoot: On flake, add explicit finds with timeouts and isolate shared state.
integration test.integration: 1) Critical path ITs. 2) Device CI. 3) Stable finders. 4) Quarantine flakes. 5) Keep widget tests majority.

intl/ARB localization.summary: Flutter l10n uses ARB files and code generation (intl/flutter_gen) for translated strings and locales.
intl/ARB localization.problem: Hard-coded English strings block markets and cause concatenation bugs for grammar.
intl/ARB localization.mechanics: Extract strings to ARB, generate localizations, and use AppLocalizations.of(context).
intl/ARB localization.tradeoffs: Process overhead vs correctness for plurals/genders—worth it early.
intl/ARB localization.troubleshoot: If missing strings, gen not run or locale not delegated.
intl/ARB localization.integration: 1) Enable l10n. 2) ARB workflow. 3) CI gen. 4) Pseudo-locale QA. 5) RTL check.

IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.summary: Intrinsic widgets measure children's intrinsic dimensions—expensive because they may lay out children twice.
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.problem: Using intrinsics in deep trees tanks performance especially in lists.
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.mechanics: Avoid in hot paths; prefer explicit sizes, Expanded, or Align; profile if needed.
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.tradeoffs: Sometimes correct for menus; almost never inside each list row.
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.troubleshoot: If jank in layout phase, search for Intrinsics in tree.
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.example: // Prefer sized widgets over IntrinsicWidth in ListView children
IntrinsicWidth/IntrinsicHeight.integration: 1) Ban Intrinsics in lists via review. 2) Replace with constraints. 3) Profile layout. 4) Document exceptions.

isolates.summary: Isolates are Dart's memory-isolated concurrency units—use for CPU-heavy work without blocking UI isolate.
isolates.problem: Heavy JSON parse/image work on UI isolate drops frames; await does not help CPU.
isolates.mechanics: Offload CPU with Isolate.run/compute, pass transferable-ish data, keep UI isolate free.
isolates.tradeoffs: Spawn cost exists—don't isolate tiny work. Prefer async IO which already frees UI.
isolates.troubleshoot: If still janky, work remains on UI or isolate messaging too large copies.
isolates.integration: 1) Profile UI isolate. 2) Isolate.run for CPU. 3) Measure. 4) Avoid for tiny tasks. 5) Error handling.

json_serializable.summary: json_serializable generates fromJson/toJson for annotated Dart classes via build_runner.
json_serializable.problem: Hand-written JSON maps drift and throw on null/type mismatches late.
json_serializable.mechanics: Annotate models, generate, parse at boundaries, and fail fast on schema mismatch.
json_serializable.tradeoffs: Codegen safety vs build_runner cost; freezed often pairs well.
json_serializable.troubleshoot: If field null errors, codegen outdated—rebuild.
json_serializable.integration: 1) Add codegen. 2) Model DTOs. 3) CI generate. 4) Strict nulls. 5) Version API adapters.

Key.summary: Keys (ValueKey/ObjectKey/UniqueKey/GlobalKey) tell Flutter which Element to match when reordering/updating widgets.
Key.problem: Index-based identity loses State on reorder; UniqueKey every build remounts always.
Key.mechanics: Assign ValueKey with stable business ids on list children that hold State.
Key.tradeoffs: Keys solve identity; they are not for styling. Don't over-key static children.
Key.troubleshoot: If form fields shuffle values after reorder, fix keys.
Key.example: ListView.builder(itemBuilder: (_, i) => TodoRow(key: ValueKey(todos[i].id), todo: todos[i]));
Key.integration: 1) Audit list keys. 2) Stable ids. 3) Widget tests reorder. 4) Reserve GlobalKey.

large Flutter app modularization.summary: Large Flutter apps split into packages/features with clear APIs to keep build times and ownership manageable.
large Flutter app modularization.problem: One giant lib/ with circular imports slows teams and analysis.
large Flutter app modularization.mechanics: Extract features into packages, enforce import boundaries, and use melos for scripts.
large Flutter app modularization.tradeoffs: More packages help scale; over-splitting early adds friction.
large Flutter app modularization.troubleshoot: If analyzer slow, modularize hot packages and reduce barrel exports.
large Flutter app modularization.integration: 1) Identify features. 2) Extract packages. 3) Boundary lint. 4) Melos CI. 5) Keep shared slim.

layout phase.summary: Layout assigns sizes/positions under constraints; expensive intrinsic/measuring layouts cause jank.
layout phase.problem: shrinkWrap lists and Intrinsics force extra layout work.
layout phase.mechanics: Avoid shrinkWrap/intrinsics in hot paths, set itemExtent when possible, and profile layout.
layout phase.tradeoffs: Correct layout vs cost—sometimes explicit sizes win.
layout phase.integration: 1) Remove shrinkWrap where Expanded works. 2) itemExtent. 3) Ban Intrinsics in lists. 4) Profile.

LayoutBuilder.summary: LayoutBuilder rebuilds its builder with the parent's incoming BoxConstraints—enabling responsive branching.
LayoutBuilder.problem: MediaQuery-only breakpoints ignore that a widget may live in a narrow sidebar.
LayoutBuilder.mechanics: Branch UI on constraints, keep builders light, and combine with flexible layouts.
LayoutBuilder.tradeoffs: Powerful for components; overusing nested LayoutBuilders adds rebuild noise.
LayoutBuilder.troubleshoot: If always getting unbounded, parent passed unbounded constraints—wrap properly.
LayoutBuilder.integration: 1) Replace viewport-only assumptions. 2) Adaptive components. 3) Test in sidebars. 4) Keep builders cheap.

ListView.summary: ListView lazily builds children in a scrollable viewport—default for vertical collections.
ListView.problem: ListView(children: hugeList) builds eagerly; shrinkWrap inside Column causes expensive layouts.
ListView.mechanics: Use builder constructors, provide keys, consider itemExtent for perf, avoid shrinkWrap when Expanded works.
ListView.tradeoffs: ListView is simple; CustomScrollView needed for mixed slivers.
ListView.troubleshoot: If jank on scroll, reduce item build cost and avoid shrinkWrap.
ListView.example: ListView.builder(itemCount: n, itemBuilder: (_, i) => Item(key: ValueKey(ids[i]), index: i));
ListView.integration: 1) Always builder for long lists. 2) Keys. 3) Expanded not shrinkWrap. 4) Profile. 5) itemExtent when uniform.

Material 3 theming.summary: Material 3 theming uses ColorScheme, TextTheme, and component themes for systematic styling.
Material 3 theming.problem: Hard-coded colors ignore dark mode and accessibility contrast.
Material 3 theming.mechanics: Define seed/scheme, apply Theme, prefer theme colors in widgets, and support dark/light.
Material 3 theming.tradeoffs: M3 defaults may differ from brand—override component themes rather than one-off colors.
Material 3 theming.troubleshoot: If dark mode breaks, missing ColorScheme roles—audit hard-coded Color(0x..).
Material 3 theming.integration: 1) Adopt M3 ThemeData. 2) Map brand tokens. 3) Dark scheme. 4) Ban raw colors in widgets. 5) Contrast check.

memory profiling.summary: Memory profiling uses DevTools heap snapshots/allocation tracing to find leaks and bloat.
memory profiling.problem: Ignoring memory causes OOM on low-end devices after long sessions.
memory profiling.mechanics: Snapshot before/after flows, follow retainers, fix listeners/images/caches.
memory profiling.troubleshoot: If size climbs after pop routes, leaked elements/subscriptions.
memory profiling.integration: 1) Baseline. 2) Diff journeys. 3) Fix retainers. 4) Automate smoke memory checks when possible.

MethodChannel.summary: MethodChannel invokes platform methods (Android/iOS) with async results—classic Flutter platform interop.
MethodChannel.problem: Missing native implementations or wrong channel names throw MissingPluginException.
MethodChannel.mechanics: Define channel string, implement handlers natively, invoke from Dart, and handle errors.
MethodChannel.tradeoffs: Channels are flexible; Pigeon adds type safety. Heavy traffic may need EventChannel/FFI.
MethodChannel.troubleshoot: If MissingPluginException, plugin not registered or running on unsupported platform.
MethodChannel.example:
const ch = MethodChannel('app.battery');
final level = await ch.invokeMethod<int>('getBatteryLevel');
MethodChannel.integration: 1) Define API. 2) Implement native. 3) Dart invoke. 4) Tests/mocks. 5) Consider Pigeon if growing.

mixins.summary: Mixins reuse implementation across class hierarchies (`with`) without deep inheritance.
mixins.problem: Mixin hell and conflicting members create fragile classes.
mixins.mechanics: Use mixins for cross-cutting State capabilities (TickerProvider), prefer composition for domain.
mixins.tradeoffs: Handy for Flutter State; overuse obscures behavior.
mixins.integration: 1) Limit mixins to framework patterns. 2) Compose domain. 3) Review conflicts. 4) Document mixin contracts.

mocking.summary: Mocks/fakes replace dependencies in tests (mockito/mocktail) to assert interactions and stub responses.
mocking.problem: Over-mocking couples tests to implementation and misses integration bugs.
mocking.mechanics: Fake repositories for VM tests, verify critical calls, and keep some integration tests unmocked.
mocking.tradeoffs: Mocks speed tests but can green-wash broken wiring.
mocking.troubleshoot: If tests pass but app fails, too many mocks—add integration coverage.
mocking.example:
when(() => api.load()).thenAnswer((_) async => sample);
verify(() => api.load()).called(1);
mocking.integration: 1) Fake repos. 2) mocktail. 3) Verify key interactions. 4) Balance with ITs. 5) Avoid mocking types you own unnecessarily.

MVVM.summary: MVVM structures Flutter apps with Views (widgets), ViewModels (state/commands), and Models (data).
MVVM.problem: Fat widgets mixing IO and UI become untestable.
MVVM.mechanics: Put state in ChangeNotifier/Cubit ViewModels, inject repositories, and keep widgets declarative.
MVVM.tradeoffs: MVVM clarity vs extra layers for tiny apps—scale the pattern to team size.
MVVM.troubleshoot: If widgets call APIs directly, move to VM/repository.
MVVM.example: class LoginVm extends ChangeNotifier { /* state + submit() */ }
MVVM.integration: 1) Introduce VM for a screen. 2) Inject repos. 3) Unit-test VM. 4) Thin widgets. 5) Consistent folder layout.

Navigator 1.0.summary: Navigator 1.0 manages a stack of Routes with push/pop and imperative APIs many apps still use.
Navigator 1.0.problem: Passing wrong context (below Navigator) fails; not awaiting results loses return values.
Navigator 1.0.mechanics: Push routes with MaterialPageRoute/named routes, pop with results, and keep a clear routing table.
Navigator 1.0.tradeoffs: 1.0 is simple; complex deep links/web sync often need Router 2.0/go_router.
Navigator 1.0.troubleshoot: If push fails, context lacks Navigator—use root navigator or correct context.
Navigator 1.0.integration: 1) Centralize routes. 2) Type results. 3) Handle back. 4) Migrate to go_router when deep links demand.

nested scrolling.summary: Nested scrolling coordinates parent/child scrollables (e.g., header + list) via NestedScrollView or custom physics.
nested scrolling.problem: Competing scrollables steal gestures and produce sticky weirdness.
nested scrolling.mechanics: Prefer CustomScrollView slivers or NestedScrollView; avoid shrinkWrap nested ListViews.
nested scrolling.tradeoffs: NestedScrollView helps but is complex; slivers often simpler.
nested scrolling.troubleshoot: If outer won't scroll, primary/controller conflict—align controllers.
nested scrolling.integration: 1) Prefer single CustomScrollView. 2) Else NestedScrollView. 3) Test gestures. 4) Avoid nested shrinkWrap.

offline-first mobile app.summary: Offline-first apps read/write a local source of truth and sync to network when available.
offline-first mobile app.problem: Online-only mobile UX fails in tunnels/planes and feels fragile.
offline-first mobile app.mechanics: Persist locally first, enqueue mutations, sync with backoff, and show sync state honestly.
offline-first mobile app.tradeoffs: Complexity vs UX—start with read-cache before full bidirectional sync.
offline-first mobile app.troubleshoot: If duplicates after sync, missing idempotency keys.
offline-first mobile app.example: // write local → outbox row → worker POST with idempotency key → mark synced
offline-first mobile app.integration: 1) Local DB. 2) Outbox. 3) Sync worker. 4) Conflict policy. 5) UX for pending/failed.

offline-first synchronization.summary: Sync protocols move local mutations to server and merge remote changes with clear conflict rules.
offline-first synchronization.problem: Last-write-wins without vector clocks/versions silently drops user edits.
offline-first synchronization.mechanics: Pull remote since cursor, push outbox with versions, resolve conflicts per domain rules.
offline-first synchronization.tradeoffs: Perfect sync is hard; pick domain-appropriate conflicts (merge fields vs LWW).
offline-first synchronization.troubleshoot: If data ping-pongs, clocks/versions wrong—add tests for concurrent edits.
offline-first synchronization.integration: 1) Define conflict policy. 2) Version fields. 3) Cursor pull. 4) Outbox push. 5) Concurrent edit tests.

package maintenance evaluation.summary: Evaluating Flutter packages checks maintenance, Flutter compatibility, issue health, and license fit.
package maintenance evaluation.problem: Adopting abandoned plugins blocks engine upgrades.
package maintenance evaluation.mechanics: Inspect pub.dev, repo activity, open critical issues, and prefer endorsed/popular maintained packages.
package maintenance evaluation.tradeoffs: Vendor vs write-your-own—estimate replacement cost before adopting.
package maintenance evaluation.troubleshoot: If plugin breaks on Flutter upgrade, check issues and be ready to fork/replace.
package maintenance evaluation.example: // Checklist: last publish, open PRs, license, platforms supported, example runs
package maintenance evaluation.integration: 1) Score candidates. 2) Spike upgrade. 3) Abstraction layer. 4) Monitor releases. 5) Exit plan.

Pigeon.summary: Pigeon generates type-safe platform channel code from a Dart API definition for Flutter↔native.
Pigeon.problem: Hand-written channels drift types and codecs between platforms.
Pigeon.mechanics: Define API, generate Dart/Kotlin/Swift, implement native hosts, call generated Dart APIs.
Pigeon.tradeoffs: Type safety vs setup cost; worth it as channel surface grows.
Pigeon.troubleshoot: If codegen mismatches, clean and regenerate; versions must align.
Pigeon.integration: 1) Write pigeon API. 2) Generate. 3) Implement hosts. 4) CI codegen. 5) Version carefully.

Provider.summary: Provider exposes values/ChangeNotifiers via InheritedWidget wrappers with convenient read/watch APIs.
Provider.problem: Using Provider.of with listen:true indiscriminately rebuilds large subtrees.
Provider.mechanics: Provide at subtree root, watch selectively, call notifyListeners on changes, dispose notifiers.
Provider.tradeoffs: Simple and popular; Riverpod addresses some test/compile-time issues. Don't provide everything globally.
Provider.troubleshoot: If rebuild storms, you watched too high—narrow Consumer/select.
Provider.integration: 1) Provide feature models. 2) watch narrowly. 3) read in callbacks. 4) Dispose. 5) Widget tests with overrides.

R8/ProGuard.summary: R8 shrinks/obfuscates Android release builds; keep rules preserve reflection-needed classes (plugins).
R8/ProGuard.problem: Missing keep rules crash release-only when Gson/reflection plugins break.
R8/ProGuard.mechanics: Enable minify for release, add plugin keep rules, save mapping for crash deobfuscation.
R8/ProGuard.tradeoffs: Smaller apps vs fragile reflection; test release builds always.
R8/ProGuard.troubleshoot: If release crash only, check mapping and missing keeps.
R8/ProGuard.integration: 1) Enable R8. 2) Add keeps. 3) Test release. 4) Upload mapping. 5) Monitor crashlytics.

real-time chat app in Flutter.summary: Realtime chat in Flutter combines socket/stream repos, local cache, optimistic UI, and notification wakeups.
real-time chat app in Flutter.problem: Polling feels laggy; no local cache blanks the chat on reopen.
real-time chat app in Flutter.mechanics: Persist messages, subscribe to room stream, reconcile acks, and virtualize long lists.
real-time chat app in Flutter.troubleshoot: If duplicates, dedupe by server id; if reorder, sort stable timestamps.
real-time chat app in Flutter.integration: 1) Message schema. 2) Local cache. 3) Socket stream. 4) Optimistic UI. 5) Push + pagination.

rebuild optimization.summary: Rebuild optimization reduces work by splitting widgets, using const, selectors, and avoiding rebuilding huge subtrees.
rebuild optimization.problem: Mega build methods rebuild charts/lists on every keystroke.
rebuild optimization.mechanics: Isolate frequently changing state, const static subtrees, and profile rebuilds before memo hacks.
rebuild optimization.troubleshoot: DevTools rebuild highlights show hot widgets—split them.
rebuild optimization.example: context.select<Cart,int>((c) => c.count); // rebuild only on count
rebuild optimization.integration: 1) Profile rebuilds. 2) Split. 3) select/watch narrow. 4) const. 5) Re-measure.

records and patterns.summary: Dart records and patterns enable concise multi-value returns and expressive switches/destructuring.
records and patterns.problem: Boilerplate classes for tiny tuples clutter APIs.
records and patterns.mechanics: Return records for small tuples, switch on sealed types with patterns, keep public domain models named when meaningful.
records and patterns.tradeoffs: Records are handy; named classes still better for evolving domain entities.
records and patterns.troubleshoot: If exhaustiveness fails, missing case—handle or use default carefully.
records and patterns.example:
final (user, token) = await login();
switch (state) { case Loading() => ...; case Ready(:final user) => ...; }
records and patterns.integration: 1) Adopt records for tuples. 2) Pattern switches on unions. 3) Keep domain named. 4) Enable exhaustive lint.

RenderFlex overflow.summary: RenderFlex overflow (yellow/black stripes) means Row/Column children exceeded available space along main axis.
RenderFlex overflow.problem: Unbounded text or fixed widths in narrow layouts ignore constraints.
RenderFlex overflow.mechanics: Wrap with Flexible/Expanded, allow text to ellipsize, or scroll; never ignore overflow in production.
RenderFlex overflow.tradeoffs: Overflow is a layout bug, not a visual style—fix constraints.
RenderFlex overflow.troubleshoot: Use Inspector to see who forced oversized child.
RenderFlex overflow.integration: 1) Reproduce narrow sizes. 2) Fix flex/text. 3) Add golden/widget tests at small sizes. 4) Ban ignore overflow.

RenderObject.summary: RenderObjects perform layout and painting; widgets configure them via Elements.
RenderObject.problem: App developers rarely need custom RenderObjects—mistakes break constraints contracts.
RenderObject.mechanics: Prefer composing widgets; write custom RenderBox only when existing render objects can't express the layout.
RenderObject.tradeoffs: Ultimate control vs maintenance cost and a11y complexity.
RenderObject.troubleshoot: If asserts in performLayout, constraints protocol violated.
RenderObject.example: // Prefer CustomPainter/box widgets before custom RenderBox
RenderObject.integration: 1) Exhaust widget options. 2) Study RenderBox docs. 3) Implement carefully. 4) Heavy tests. 5) Semantics.

RepaintBoundary.summary: RepaintBoundary creates a separate display list layer so frequent repaints don't dirty siblings.
RepaintBoundary.problem: Animating one subtree without boundaries can repaint large ancestors costlessly avoided.
RepaintBoundary.mechanics: Wrap chatty animations/complex static siblings strategically; don't wrap everything.
RepaintBoundary.tradeoffs: More layers help repaint isolation but use memory/GPU bandwidth.
RepaintBoundary.troubleshoot: If still janky, problem may be build/layout not paint—check timeline.
RepaintBoundary.integration: 1) Profile paints. 2) Boundary around static vs animated. 3) Re-measure. 4) Avoid excessive layers.

repository pattern.summary: Repositories abstract data sources (API/DB) behind interfaces consumed by VMs/use-cases.
repository pattern.problem: Widgets calling dio/Firebase directly scatter caching and error mapping.
repository pattern.mechanics: Define repo interfaces, implement with remote/local, inject into VMs, fake in tests.
repository pattern.tradeoffs: Clear boundaries vs extra layer for tiny apps—use when multiple sources appear.
repository pattern.troubleshoot: If swapping API breaks UI, mapping leaked—keep DTOs inside repo.
repository pattern.example:
abstract class TodoRepo { Future<List<Todo>> list(); }
class ApiTodoRepo implements TodoRepo { /* dio */ }
repository pattern.integration: 1) Repo interfaces. 2) Impl remote/local. 3) Inject. 4) Fake tests. 5) Map errors once.

REST API integration.summary: Flutter REST integration uses http/dio clients, DTO parsing, auth headers, and resilient error mapping.
REST API integration.problem: Parsing JSON in UI isolates janks; ignoring non-2xx statuses mis-handles errors.
REST API integration.mechanics: Centralize client, parse with json_serializable, map errors, and optionally isolate heavy parses.
REST API integration.tradeoffs: dio features vs http simplicity—pick one and standardize.
REST API integration.troubleshoot: If UI janks on large JSON, move parse off UI isolate.
REST API integration.example:
final res = await http.get(uri, headers: headers);
if (res.statusCode >= 400) throw ApiException(res.statusCode);
REST API integration.integration: 1) API client module. 2) Typed DTOs. 3) Error mapping. 4) Auth refresh. 5) Widget/repo tests.

retry/backoff.summary: Client retry with exponential backoff+jitter handles transient mobile network failures.
retry/backoff.problem: Immediate retries drain battery and hammer recovering servers.
retry/backoff.mechanics: Retry GETs and idempotent writes, honor Retry-After, and queue when offline.
retry/backoff.tradeoffs: Retries improve resilience; non-idempotent POSTs need keys.
retry/backoff.troubleshoot: If storms in logs, missing jitter/caps.
retry/backoff.example: await retry(() => client.get(url), maxAttempts: 5, delayFactor: Duration(ms: 200));
retry/backoff.integration: 1) Classify idempotent calls. 2) Backoff+jitter. 3) Honor Retry-After. 4) Metrics. 5) UX for final failure.

Riverpod.summary: Riverpod is a compile-safe reactive caching/state toolkit that improves on Provider with no BuildContext for reads.
Riverpod.problem: Provider context lookup limitations and disposal bugs push teams to Riverpod.
Riverpod.mechanics: Declare providers globally, watch in consumers, use autoDispose for ephemeral state, override in tests.
Riverpod.tradeoffs: Learning curve vs safety; still don't put all ephemeral UI flags in providers.
Riverpod.troubleshoot: If disposed provider errors, lifecycle mismatch—tune autoDispose.
Riverpod.integration: 1) Add Riverpod. 2) Migrate one feature. 3) autoDispose where needed. 4) Override in tests. 5) Document provider graph.

Row and Column.summary: Row and Column are Flex widgets laying out children horizontally/vertically under incoming constraints.
Row and Column.problem: Placing unbounded scroll views inside them without Expanded causes layout exceptions.
Row and Column.mechanics: Choose axis, align children, expand to fill leftover space, and respect constraints.
Row and Column.tradeoffs: Simple and ubiquitous; complex grids may need Wrap/GridView/CustomMultiChildLayout.
Row and Column.troubleshoot: Overflow? Check Expanded and text wrapping.
Row and Column.integration: 1) Standardize spacing. 2) Expanded patterns. 3) Test small screens. 4) Prefer Wrap when needed.

SafeArea.summary: SafeArea pads children to avoid system OS intrusions (notches, status bar, home indicator).
SafeArea.problem: Content under notches looks broken and can be untappable.
SafeArea.mechanics: Wrap top-level scaffolds/screens with SafeArea or use padded AppBars that handle insets.
SafeArea.tradeoffs: Sometimes intentional edge-to-edge design needs manual padding instead of SafeArea everywhere.
SafeArea.troubleshoot: If double padding, SafeArea + AppBar both applied—disable edges.
SafeArea.integration: 1) Apply SafeArea at screen roots. 2) Verify devices with notches. 3) Handle keyboards. 4) Edge-to-edge carefully.

ScrollController.summary: ScrollController observes/drives scroll offset for infinite scroll, parallax, and scroll-to-index patterns.
ScrollController.problem: Sharing one controller across multiple scrollables or forgetting dispose leaks.
ScrollController.mechanics: Create controller in State, attach to one scrollable, listen for thresholds, dispose.
ScrollController.tradeoffs: Controller gives power; NotificationListener often enough for simple cases.
ScrollController.troubleshoot: If 'ScrollController attached to multiple', reuse bug—one controller per scrollable.
ScrollController.integration: 1) Own controller in State. 2) Dispose. 3) Infinite scroll guards. 4) Tests with controller jumps.

sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.summary: Dart class modifiers (sealed/base/interface/final) control where types can be implemented/extended for safer APIs.
sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.problem: Open hierarchies allow unexpected subtypes that break switch exhaustiveness assumptions.
sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.mechanics: Mark state unions sealed, lock library types with base/final as needed, and switch exhaustively.
sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.tradeoffs: Stricter APIs help large codebases; may constrain plugin authors—document.
sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.troubleshoot: If outside subtype appears, modifier missing—tighten.
sealed/base/interface/final class modifi.integration: 1) Seal state unions. 2) Exhaustive switches. 3) final leaf types. 4) Document intended extension points.

secure token storage.summary: Secure token storage uses Keychain/Keystore-backed plugins (flutter_secure_storage) instead of plain prefs.
secure token storage.problem: Tokens in SharedPreferences are readable on rooted/jailbroken devices and backups sometimes.
secure token storage.mechanics: Store refresh tokens securely, short-lived access in memory when possible, wipe on logout.
secure token storage.tradeoffs: Secure storage still not perfect on compromised devices—pair with server revocation.
secure token storage.troubleshoot: If tokens vanish on upgrade, storage options/accessibility settings wrong.
secure token storage.integration: 1) Secure storage plugin. 2) Memory for access token. 3) Logout wipe. 4) Jailbreak heuristics optional. 5) Revoke server-side.

Semantics.summary: Semantics describe UI meaning for assistive technologies; Flutter merges a semantics tree parallel to widgets.
Semantics.problem: Custom painted controls without semantics are invisible to TalkBack/VoiceOver.
Semantics.mechanics: Use semantic widgets (button/text), add Semantics for custom controls, and test with screen readers.
Semantics.tradeoffs: Too many semantics nodes can confuse; merge thoughtfully.
Semantics.troubleshoot: If unlabeled buttons, wrap with Semantics(button:true, label:...).
Semantics.example: Semantics(label: 'Delete item', button: true, onTap: onDelete, child: Icon(Icons.delete));
Semantics.integration: 1) Audit custom controls. 2) Labels/actions. 3) SR testing. 4) Keep Material semantics where possible.

setState.summary: setState marks the Element dirty so Flutter rebuilds that State's widget subtree with new fields.
setState.problem: Calling setState after dispose or for every tiny leaf without splitting causes crashes/jank.
setState.mechanics: Update fields and call setState, guard with mounted, and split widgets so setState scope stays small.
setState.tradeoffs: Fine for local UI; escalate to app state libs when sharing across routes.
setState.troubleshoot: If setState() called after dispose(), async gap—check mounted.
setState.integration: 1) Local state via setState. 2) mounted guards. 3) Split trees. 4) Move shared state up/out.

setState after dispose.summary: setState after dispose happens when async callbacks complete after State unmount—framework asserts in debug.
setState after dispose.problem: Missing mounted checks crash or spam logs when users navigate away quickly.
setState after dispose.mechanics: Track subscriptions, cancel in dispose, and check mounted before setState after awaits.
setState after dispose.tradeoffs: Always a bug to ignore—fix ownership of async work.
setState after dispose.troubleshoot: Reproduce by popping during in-flight request; add guards.
setState after dispose.integration: 1) Audit async State methods. 2) mounted checks. 3) Cancel subs. 4) Regression tests fast pop.

SharedPreferences.summary: SharedPreferences stores small key-value prefs locally (NSUserDefaults/SharedPreferences).
SharedPreferences.problem: Storing secrets or large blobs here is insecure/slow; async API misuse assumes sync availability.
SharedPreferences.mechanics: Await instance, read/write simple prefs, and use secure storage for tokens.
SharedPreferences.tradeoffs: Simple prefs vs need for typed DB—don't stretch it.
SharedPreferences.troubleshoot: If null unexpectedly, key mismatch or cleared app data.
SharedPreferences.example:
final p = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
await p.setBool('dark', true);
SharedPreferences.integration: 1) Prefs for UX flags only. 2) Secure tokens elsewhere. 3) Default values. 4) Document keys.

sound null safety.summary: Sound null safety makes nullable types explicit so the analyzer proves null dereferences can't occur.
sound null safety.mechanics: Model nullability honestly, promote with checks, avoid ! except when proven, prefer late only for definite assignment.
sound null safety.tradeoffs: Migration pain vs runtime crash reduction—worth it fully.
sound null safety.troubleshoot: If bang throws, the assumption was wrong—model nullable instead.
sound null safety.integration: 1) Full null safety. 2) Ban unnecessary !. 3) Strict lints. 4) Fix rather than bang.

SQLite/sqflite.summary: sqflite is a popular SQLite plugin for local relational storage on mobile.
SQLite/sqflite.problem: No migrations strategy corrupts upgrades; main-isolate heavy queries jank UI.
SQLite/sqflite.mechanics: Open with version+onUpgrade, wrap multi-writes in transactions, index query columns, consider background isolates.
SQLite/sqflite.tradeoffs: SQL control vs Drift's codegen convenience.
SQLite/sqflite.troubleshoot: If upgrade crashes, onUpgrade incomplete—test migrations on copies.
SQLite/sqflite.example:
await db.execute('CREATE TABLE ...');
await db.transaction((txn) async { /* ... */ });
SQLite/sqflite.integration: 1) Schema+migrations. 2) Indexes. 3) Transactions. 4) Offload heavy queries. 5) Backup strategy.

State lifecycle.summary: StatefulWidget State mounts via initState, updates via didUpdateWidget, cleans in deactivate/dispose.
State lifecycle.problem: Starting streams in build or skipping dispose leaks and duplicates subscriptions.
State lifecycle.mechanics: Init controllers/subscriptions in initState, respond to prop changes in didUpdateWidget, dispose all.
State lifecycle.tradeoffs: Lifecycle mastery prevents leaks; prefer higher-level state managers for complex syncing.
State lifecycle.troubleshoot: If double subscription, initState work incorrectly re-run—check keys remounting.
State lifecycle.integration: 1) Audit dispose. 2) No side effects in build. 3) Tests for remount. 4) Document owned resources.

StatelessWidget.summary: StatelessWidget describes UI from configuration (props) without local mutable State.
StatelessWidget.problem: Pushing ephemeral interaction state into parents unnecessarily creates rebuild churn.
StatelessWidget.mechanics: Prefer const Stateless widgets; escalate to Stateful/Cubit when local mutable state appears.
StatelessWidget.tradeoffs: Stateless clarity vs needing State for animations/forms.
StatelessWidget.troubleshoot: If you need setState, it's no longer Stateless—migrate.
StatelessWidget.integration: 1) Prefer const Stateless. 2) Elevate state intentionally. 3) Const all the way. 4) Lint unnecessary stateful.

Stream.summary: Streams deliver asynchronous sequences of events—used for sockets, Firestore snapshots, and BLoC.
Stream.problem: Missing cancellation leaks; using single-subscription streams twice throws.
Stream.mechanics: Subscribe with StreamBuilder or listen+cancel, choose broadcast when multi-listen needed, handle errors.
Stream.tradeoffs: Streams are powerful; Futures suffice for one-shot. Backpressure rarely automatic—careful producers.
Stream.troubleshoot: If 'already listened', need broadcast or new instance per listener.
Stream.integration: 1) StreamBuilder for UI. 2) Cancel elsewhere. 3) Error UI. 4) Prefer broadcast for multi fans. 5) Test cancellation.

unit test.summary: Flutter unit tests verify pure Dart logic (VMs, parsers) quickly without rendering.
unit test.problem: Putting logic only in widgets forces slower widget tests for everything.
unit test.mechanics: Extract logic to testable classes and assert outputs/errors with fakes.
unit test.tradeoffs: Unit vs widget/integration—pyramid with mostly unit.
unit test.troubleshoot: If needing WidgetsFlutterBinding for pure logic, logic not extracted yet.
unit test.integration: 1) Extract logic. 2) Unit tests. 3) Fake repos. 4) Keep CI fast. 5) Widget tests for UI wiring.

ValueNotifier.summary: ValueNotifier is a ChangeNotifier holding a single value—lightweight reactive cell for small local state.
ValueNotifier.problem: Using full Provider/BLoC for a single boolean can be ceremony overkill.
ValueNotifier.mechanics: Create notifier, rebuild with ValueListenableBuilder, dispose with owner.
ValueNotifier.tradeoffs: Tiny and fast; not a full app architecture. Combine with larger patterns as needed.
ValueNotifier.troubleshoot: If UI not updating, you mutated fields inside value without reassigning value.
ValueNotifier.example:
final open = ValueNotifier(false);
ValueListenableBuilder(valueListenable: open, builder: ...);
ValueNotifier.integration: 1) Use for local leaf state. 2) Dispose. 3) Escalate to Cubit when logic grows. 4) Prefer immutable value replaces.

Wasm/SkWasm.summary: Skwasm is Flutter web's Wasm-oriented rendering path aiming for smaller/faster web engines than classic CanvasKit loading.
Wasm/SkWasm.problem: Large Wasm downloads still hurt first load if not cached/deferred thoughtfully.
Wasm/SkWasm.mechanics: Build with current Flutter web Wasm options, test target browsers, measure load.
Wasm/SkWasm.troubleshoot: If blank on older browsers, feature unsupported—detect and fallback.
Wasm/SkWasm.example: flutter build web --wasm  # per current Flutter docs/flags
Wasm/SkWasm.integration: 1) Evaluate Wasm builds. 2) Browser matrix. 3) Measure. 4) Fallback plan. 5) Cache aggressively.

WebSocket.summary: WebSockets give Flutter apps bidirectional realtime channels for chat/presence.
WebSocket.problem: No reconnect/backoff drops users on mobile networks; parsing on UI isolate janks.
WebSocket.mechanics: Connect with auth, heartbeat, exponential reconnect, and push events into a repository stream.
WebSocket.tradeoffs: Sockets are great for chat; SSE may suffice for server→client only.
WebSocket.troubleshoot: If battery drain, too-aggressive reconnect/ping—tune intervals.
WebSocket.integration: 1) Repo-level socket. 2) Auth. 3) Reconnect+backoff. 4) Offline queue. 5) Profile parse cost.

Widget.summary: Widgets are immutable configuration objects describing UI; Flutter rebuilds them cheaply compared to Elements/RenderObjects.
Widget.problem: Mutating widgets or heavy build methods without const causes avoidable work.
Widget.mechanics: Compose small widgets, use const, and keep build pure and light.
Widget.tradeoffs: Fine-grained widgets help rebuild control but too many layers hurt readability.
Widget.troubleshoot: If rebuild expensive, split widgets and add const.
Widget.integration: 1) Const-friendly widgets. 2) Split builds. 3) Pure build. 4) Profile rebuilds.

Widget tree.summary: The widget tree is the immutable configuration hierarchy Flutter diffs each build to update elements.
Widget tree.problem: Deep unnecessary subtrees and missing keys make diffs remount too much.
Widget tree.mechanics: Keep trees intentional, key stateful lists, and inspect with Widget Inspector.
Widget tree.tradeoffs: Deeper trees vs fewer large builds—split when profiling says so.
Widget tree.troubleshoot: Inspector highlights rebuilds—use it when optimizing.
Widget tree.integration: 1) Learn inspector. 2) Key lists. 3) Split heavy builds. 4) Avoid mega-build methods.

zones.summary: Zones provide overriding execution contexts for async error handling and forkable behaviors in Dart.
zones.problem: Uncaught async errors outside runZonedGuarded escape to the console without reporting.
zones.mechanics: Wrap app startup in runZonedGuarded to report errors, careful with zone-crossing assumptions.
zones.tradeoffs: Zones are powerful/low-level—prefer framework error hooks when enough.
zones.troubleshoot: If errors missing in Crashlytics, zone/handler not installed early enough.
zones.integration: 1) Guard main. 2) Report to crash tool. 3) FlutterError.onError too. 4) Test intentional throws.
